findings.summary: An audit trail is a security-relevant chronological record of activities affecting a system, operation, or device. It is typically generated in privileged mode to supervise all user actions, with the trail data protected from normal user modification. Industries apply audit trails to track financial transactions, support regulatory compliance, enable forensic investigation, and maintain procedural accountability in fields ranging from healthcare to employment.

mechanisms.title: Privileged-mode generation
mechanisms.explanation: The process creating an audit trail is required to run in privileged mode so it can access and supervise all user actions. Normal users should not be allowed to stop or change the trail.

mechanisms.title: Access restriction and role-based security
mechanisms.explanation: Audit trail data should not be accessible to normal users. A role-based security model in the software can handle this protection, ensuring the trail file or database table remains restricted.

unknowns: Exact technical implementation of closed-loop controls in all software
Whether all audit trail systems use cryptographic integrity verification
Details of real-time log review intervals beyond stated regulatory guidance
Specific mechanisms for audit trail generation in legacy or proprietary systems
